subject: Clarification on hosted log ephemerality, residency, and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-med.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@acme-med.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: where are prompts/outputs kept by default?

Hi Marissa,

We’re finalizing our security questionnaire and I need a concise account of Redwood’s default behaviour for hosted logs: specifically where raw prompts, model outputs, and request/response metadata are stored by default, and what the default retention windows are. Our privacy team also wants to understand the deletion workflow (how to trigger a complete purge, and expected propagation delays).

A couple of constraints to highlight: we must keep customer data in the US region only, and we’d like an option to avoid storing raw prompts at all unless we explicitly opt in.

Can you summarize defaults and the configuration knobs available in the Console or via API?

Thanks — Alice
Alice Chen
Director, Clinical AI — Acme Medical
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-med.com>
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@acme-med.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are prompts/outputs kept by default?

Alice —

Thanks for the clear constraints. Below is a short, actionable summary tailored to Acme Medical (US-only residency):

1) Default storage and residency
- Hosted API (default account): request metadata (timestamps, route, token counts) + redacted prompt fingerprints are stored for 45 days in the regional data store. For US accounts that are region-mapped, these artifacts remain in US datacenters by default.
- Raw prompts and full model outputs (i.e., the literal request text and generated text) are retained in a short-lived debug store by default for 14 days. This store is also region-mapped for the account.
- Dedicated and Private deployments: data residency and retention are customer-controlled; defaults are the customer’s responsibility (we do not importally copy logs to hosted storage).

2) Why two windows?
- The 14-day raw-text window allows transient troubleshooting and quality investigations while limiting exposure. The 45-day metadata window is for billing reconciliation, metrics, and aggregated telemetry without preserving raw user text beyond the shorter window.

3) Opt-outs / configuration knobs
- Console: Settings > Data & Retention lets you set "Raw prompt storage" to Off (prevents raw prompts/outputs from being stored after request completion) and to select regional residency (US/EU/APAC).
- API: /v1/account/retention (PATCH) supports: raw_prompt_storage: [on|off|hash-only], retention_days: {debug_text: integer, metadata: integer}, region_lock: [us|eu|apac].
- When raw_prompt_storage=hash-only we keep SHA256 hashes for dedup/quality tooling (no recoverable text).

4) Deletion / purge workflow
- Immediate purge request: Console -> Support -> "Data purge" or API: POST /v1/account/retention/purge with account_id and scope=[debug_text|metadata|all].
- Propagation: primary store purge completes within 24 hours. Asynchronous backups and analytics indices are purged within 30 days; customers receive a completion notice when all retained copies are deleted.

5) Audit & evidence
- We can provide a deletion runbook and a signed purge log (SUP-4821) for compliance review. See attached runbook and the architecture diagram for where artifacts flow.

I’m copying Neha (Security) and Rishi (Product) for any additions or hard limits we should call out for SOC2/enterprise contracts.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are prompts/outputs kept by default?

Thanks — couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec review:

1) If we set raw_prompt_storage=off, can you confirm there is zero recoverable raw text stored anywhere (including logs, debug snapshots, or long tail analytics)?
2) For retention configuration via API, does the change apply retroactively to existing stored raw prompts or only to new requests going forward?

We need these clarifications before we sign the DPA amendment.

—Paul
Paul Rivers
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Medical
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Paul Rivers <paul.rivers@acme-med.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-med.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Sep 2028 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where are prompts/outputs kept by default?

Hi Paul / Alice —

Short answers to your two bullets, and I’ll keep it tight as you’re on procurement timelines: 

1) raw_prompt_storage=off: yes — for hosted accounts that flag the setting we do not retain recoverable raw-text at request completion. Operational traces that are needed for infrastructure debugging are redacted to remove customer text before any diagnostic retention. We also ensure that any application logs that might contain request payloads are scrubbed via automated filters.

2) Retention changes: changes to retention_days or raw_prompt_storage take effect immediately for new requests. For existing stored raw prompts/outputs: an account-level retroactive purge can be initiated (Console or API purge endpoint). If you want automatic retroactive pruning when you flip the setting, we can include a clause in the DPA that triggers a bulk purge operation within 24 hours of the change — that’s what many enterprise customers choose.

Operational note: completed purges are logged and we provide a signed certificate of destruction; backups and long-tail analytics indices require up to 30 days to fully scrub.

If you’d like, I can kick off an SUP ticket to schedule a retroactive purge and provide the evidence package.

—Neha Kapoor
Security & Privacy Lead | Redwood Inference
